title: Principles of Media & Press Interviews
overview: This practical program develops the knowledge, preparation techniques and communication skills required to participate effectively in media and press interviews. Participants learn how newsrooms work, how to communicate accurate and relevant messages, and how to respond with composure to challenging questions across print, broadcast and digital channels. The program combines ethical media engagement, interview planning, message discipline, on-camera practice and constructive feedback to strengthen organizational credibility and public trust.
audience: Public relations, communications and corporate affairs professionals.
Government and institutional representatives who engage with journalists.
Executives, managers and subject-matter experts invited to give interviews.
Press officers, media relations teams and spokesperson support personnel.
Professionals responsible for public information and reputation management.
methodology: Facilitator-led discussion, analysis of real-world interview scenarios, newsroom and media-format comparisons, key-message workshops, simulated print and broadcast interviews, recorded on-camera practice, challenging-question drills, peer review, and individual feedback with a practical improvement plan.
competencies: Media literacy and understanding of journalistic practices.
Interview planning, preparation and audience analysis.
Clear, accurate and audience-centered message delivery.
Active listening, question interpretation and concise responses.
Composure, nonverbal communication and vocal presence.
Ethical communication, fact-checking and confidentiality awareness.
Managing difficult questions and correcting misinformation.
Evaluating interviews and improving future media engagement.
objectives: Explain the roles, priorities and working practices of journalists and news outlets.
Differentiate interview expectations across print, radio, television and digital media.
Assess the purpose, audience, format and risks of a proposed interview.
Prepare evidence-based key messages and supporting examples.
Respond to questions clearly while staying relevant and factually accurate.
Apply bridging and signposting techniques without evading legitimate questions.
Handle sensitive, unexpected and challenging questions professionally.
Demonstrate appropriate body language, voice and camera presence.
Recognize ethical boundaries, confidentiality obligations and approval requirements.
Evaluate recorded interviews and formulate a personal development plan.
